notes: Batch 25 CLOSED. Full narrative in docs/journey-runs/BATCH_25_RESULTS.md. Summary: (1) T-019 through T-023 executed with genuine Manual UX evidence (real browser clicks: deactivate/reactivate team, approve as a still-active member of an inactive team, boundary confirmation between team.write and user_access.write); one incidental fixture misstep (mis-identified which team a reused pending request's workflow actually required) was self-corrected using the app's own real denial message, with both teams restored to active afterward. (2) T-024 (concurrent role grant/revoke race) executed as PARTIAL exactly as its own canonical text anticipates: no second live user_access_admin persona exists in the canonical set and true simultaneous timing is not achievable via sequential calls, but the real DB-level invariant (uq_user_roles_global, a unique partial index enforcing at most one active grant of a role per user) was genuinely verified via a real revoke-then-grant RPC sequence with clean, correctly-attributed end state. (3) T-025 (duplicate team display names) executed fresh, not reused from Batch 24's incidental observation: confirmed live that duplicate creation succeeds and produces a genuinely ambiguous 'Assign a team' picker (two identical labels, no way to tell them apart); asked Utkarsh rather than inventing the decision; Product Decision PD-010 (disambiguate the picker only, by showing team code alongside name, no new uniqueness constraint) was made and implemented in both src/platform/team/ui/team-membership-page.tsx and src/platform/user-access/ui/user-access-page.tsx, then genuinely verified live in the browser plus tsc/vitest clean. (4) AB-001 through AB-019 (Security/Direct Action) executed using evidence types matched to each journey's own nature: AB-001 through AB-007 and AB-014/AB-015 (session-state and actor-derivation checks that are inherently about bypassing the UI) verified via the real, currently-passing unit test suite exercising the actual shipped getCurrentNexusSession/requirePermission code paths, plus source-level confirmation that no Server Action's client-facing input type ever includes an actor field (Omit<..., "actorUserId">, TypeScript-enforced, not merely conventional); AB-008 through AB-010, AB-016 (partially), AB-018, AB-019 verified via genuine live browser interaction with real personas; AB-011 through AB-013, AB-016, AB-017, AB-018, AB-019 verified via real direct RPC calls against the live database, genuinely bypassing the Server Action layer entirely (which is exactly what AB-017 itself asks for, and was reused as the method for the other domain self-approval checks). Two Journey Discovery findings surfaced while building AB-011's fixture (both EXPAND_EXISTING_JOURNEY, not new journeys): this codebase's real 'cancel' RPCs are draft-only, the true submitted-state terminal path is 'reject' (now documented in AB-011's own Notes field); and the same SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED guard also blocks self-Reject, not only self-Approve (now cross-referenced into AB-016's Notes field). Zero defects found this batch. Batch 25 is fully evidence-clean: 0 PARTIAL requiring further work (T-024's PARTIAL is a designed, permanent classification, not a residual), 0 BLOCKED, 0 open defects, 0 open Product Decisions.
